title: “Feelings Twitter” tries to become a jobs network
summary:
The most quotable tell in this whole saga is Qiaochu Yuan basically saying: can we PLEASE graduate from “helping each other explore our feelings” to “helping each other make money and collaborate… that feel alive, enriching, wholesome.” That June 2022 tweet is the match—suddenly everyone’s like “yes!! it’s starting!!” but when you look closely, the thread is a museum of people describing the same desire in different fonts: work that doesn’t feel like self-betrayal.

The prequel is 2021 crypto discourse: visakanv asks “if web3 is electricity, what’s the lightbulb?” and Rich Decibels answers with the big promise—“add an economic layer to your social graph,” making orgs as easy to start as a group chat. mechanical_monk dunks on it (“ah so like having a job”), and DRMacIver twists the knife: most startup work isn’t important; it’s mostly theater for funding. visakanv tries to get concrete with a “FAN microgrants” quests model (micro-scholarship content as the first quests). Then Qiaochu’s 2022 post becomes the central rally point: __drewface shows off an actual pocket of execution (NYC internet-friends-turned-roommates/cofounders, recruiting “100 people within a 5 min walk”), while rickbenger claims Bloomco_ has “made this transition” and pitches pooling dreams like a portfolio + protection from “bs jobs.”

The peak is when the thread tries to operationalize the vibe without killing it: the_wilderless argues the blocker isn’t technical, it’s “imagination and sense-of-permission,” proposing “group imaginal sessions” and later “tpot apprenticeships, skill-shares, mentorships.” vividvoid goes full institution-builder with a “metamodern wellness center… a 21st century Gymnasium” (therapy + gym + spiritual ed + workshops) and Qiaochu immediately flags the obvious failure mode—“really asking to turn into a cult tho”—to which vividvoid responds: design stopgaps; therapists manage not to become cults. The thread then sort of peters out into variations of “this is happening in pockets” and “just do the things” (AskYatharth’s critique: stop trying to shift a nebulous community; form coalitions around concrete projects).

Why care: it’s a live case study of a very 2020s problem—people who did the inner work realizing the outer work (money, projects, institutions) requires norms, boundaries, and conflict-tolerant coordination, not just vibes. The discourse keeps circling the same missing piece: everyone wants “collaboration that feels alive,” but nobody has a widely adopted template for turning trust/attunement into durable, boring systems that still don’t turn into “a job,” a startup funding pantomime, or a cult.
